features.title: The Diametric SCP
features.summary: This release is named for what it proves: three plain measures — the Demometer, the Diameter, the Muxameter — and the worked example is the Suite 8 page itself, the same page standing across locations, relaying its advances.
detail: Three terms, plain on first use. A Demometer is a different measure — a distinct part with its own measurable identity. A Diameter is a through-measure — a similarity drawn between UNLIKE parts. A Muxameter is the integrated measure — a part as it relays through the others' Diameters, proven by operation.

The worked example is this page itself. A Suite 8 page is the Demometer — and what makes two Demometers UNLIKE is the LOCATIONS of the pages: the same page standing on different SCPs. The Diameter is the locality — either location can perform from the immediate SCP: stand Local anor observe and act upon a Specified app, from right where you are. And the Muxameter forms when you work an S8 page on one SCP and cascade its advances — back into the Base the page may be formalized from, anor out to the Informatives where you find use for the page across your projects. The page as it relays, proven by the operation itself.

The entries below carry the Total. The SyncLibrary is the foundation — the locality every page holds. On it stand the teeth: Page Transfer, landing a real page on another SCP through four honest stations, and the update from any location, cascading advances into the Base anor the Informatives with divergence held for your decision. Around them, cascade memory renders live across apps, colors round-trip, textures live in each app's own library, and the Forge Menu stands on every page. Not a feature list — measures that relay. The counters read it plainly: 0.950.0 · cli 12 · scp 13 · s8 1.

THE ANOR NOTATION — anor is the Gradient Conjunctive within a Range: And anor Or anor Everything-In-Between. The working example renders here: Blue anor Yellow — and Green is within Blue anor Yellow, the way every measure in this release holds its range whole rather than forcing a choice between its ends.

features.title: The SyncLibrary — every page holds a locality
features.summary: The foundation of this release: each Suite 8 page holds a locality — stand Local anor observe a Specified app from right where you are — with a live Locality Register to choose, release, and re-arm without a reload.
detail: Each Suite 8 page carries a locality: stand Local anor observe a Specified app, from right where you are. The Locality Register lays it plain — the Local row, then the live ring rows beside it, each with its status; choose anor release a locality and re-arm it with no reload. Localities are only ever LIVE.

A fire under a Specified locality reaches the TARGET app — never a silent local fire. Content moves under fixed paths while only the library carries the intelligence, and the failure mode is always preservation of your last local truth, never adoption. Everything else in this release stands on this ground.

features.title: Suite 8 Page Transfer — the Install Circuit
features.summary: Install a Suite 8 page onto another SCP from the page's own panel — four stations, Requirements → Target → Gate → Update — landing the real page with a report written into the receiving app's own working record. Proven twice in the field.
detail: The transfer runs from the page's own panel through four stations: Requirements → Target → Gate → Update. A Requirements pass writes the page's needs and concerns into the package itself — they travel with the page, so the receiving app is told honestly what it is taking on.

The transfer lands the REAL page, with a report written into the receiving app's own working record — and a failed gate restores everything honestly, nothing left half-landed. Proven twice in the field.

features.title: The update from any location — the Base anor the Informatives
features.summary: Work an S8 page wherever you stand, and cascade its advances — back into the Base it was formalized from, anor out to the Informatives where you use it across your projects. Divergence never overwrites: both sides quoted, you decide.
detail: A Suite 8 page is no longer worked only where it was born. Work it wherever you stand and cascade the advances — back into the Base the page was formalized from, anor out to the Informatives where you find use for it across your projects. The panel names the concrete relation — Base:Name ← Informative:Name — and dispatches role-correctly.
Divergence never overwrites: where the two sides differ, the difference is held with both sides quoted and you decide. The resolved page becomes the new Base. Field-proven across two live apps.

features.title: Cascade memory, live across apps
features.summary: A page's own working memory — its cascade documents — renders in an observing app within about 100ms of the write. No reload, honest empty states, and a removal honestly cleared.
detail: Open a page's cascade documents from an observing app and what you read is the LIVE record: a write on the owning side renders in the observer within about 100ms — no reload, no stale copy. A page with no memory yet shows an honest empty state, and a removed document is honestly cleared, never left as a ghost.

features.title: Suite colors travel a full circuit
features.summary: A color choice now completes a round trip before it paints — written to the app's own configuration first, then returned to every open window at once, so what you see is always the shared truth.
detail: Pick a color and it lands in your app's hifiConfig.json before any window changes — then every window, including the one you clicked in, re-tints together on the return. No window ever shows a color the configuration does not hold.

And the circuit reaches across apps: from Pewter Tessera, choose another app's locality and set ITS colors — its own windows re-tint live, your styling stays untouched, and the swatches you edit show the target's true palette the whole time.

features.title: Suite textures become a living library
features.summary: The SVG textures behind every pane now live in each app's own patternLibrary.json — a new texture is one small JSON entry, no code change, no restart, and open pages pick it up live.
detail: Each app ships the full texture set as a seeded patternLibrary.json and can grow it freely — drop a validated entry in and the texture appears in the picker, paints on selection, and travels the same cross-app circuit colors do. A texture added while windows are open registers itself on the spot.
Rapid changes settle gracefully too: a burst of edits coalesces to the final value before it lands, so the last choice is the one that paints.

features.title: The Entourage Forge Menu, on every page
features.summary: The Forge menu now stands as its own widget on each Suite 8 page — sessions filtered to that page alone, build actions drawn from the page's own documentation, and one motion to reach the live Forge.
detail: A page's Forge menu shows only the conductions commissioned from THAT page — a fresh page starts honestly empty. Its build actions come from the page's own ForgeMenu.json when one is authored (the built-in set stands otherwise), and firing one either reaches the live Forge for that page or begins a new conduction carrying the action with it.

The widget is yours to place: remove it from any page and it stays removed — even through a page update — while the Suite 8 panel always keeps the full menu within reach. A freshly authored page opens with the menu expanded; fold it away and the page remembers.

features.title: Every page carries its own version
features.summary: A Suite 8 page now holds a version of its own — and when a newer one ships, the page's own toolbar button turns amber to say so, quietly, without touching the main version badge.
detail: Until now, only the app as a whole knew whether it was current. A Suite 8 page is a living surface — it can advance on its own cadence — so each page now carries a page version counted apart from the CLI and the app template. When the published page version outpaces the one your page carries, the page's own Suite 8 toolbar button turns amber — a signal that belongs to that page alone.

The main version badge keeps its own voice: it never turns amber for a page update, and the amber toolbar never turns the badge red. Two signals, two meanings — the badge speaks for the app, the amber toggle speaks for the page in front of you.

features.title: The page update, always within reach
features.summary: The Suite 8 Control panel now carries a standing PAGE and NPM readout with an update control beside it — refresh a single page to its latest shipped version whenever you choose.
detail: Open the Suite 8 Control panel and a plain row reads it straight: PAGE #N · NPM #M — the version your page carries beside the version the release ships. The update control stands right there, always available: you decide when a page catches up, page by page, never all-at-once by surprise.

The readout tells the truth whether or not an update waits: matching numbers mean the page is current, and the amber toggle rests. A higher NPM number is the invitation — press the control when the moment suits you.

features.title: A page update that honors your design
features.summary: A page refresh runs through the Entourage Forge with a conference first — nothing you shaped is overwritten without your say, the way every SCP update already protects your work.
detail: Refreshing a page is not a silent overwrite. It runs through the Entourage Forge, which opens a conference honoring what you have already made: where the new page and your version differ, you decide — your own design is never clobbered by a template default. The same preservation discipline the SCP update circuit stands on now guards the single page.
The Forge carries the change onto your page and lets you review it in place. Land what serves you, keep what is yours — the refresh is conducted by you, decision by decision.

features.title: The Forge's Reference Designs, renewed
features.summary: The Entourage Forge's Reference Design list gains two: Prepared Agent Dispatch — sequence any number of agents straight from your page — and OnBoard.md, so a page ships with its own onboarding.
detail: Prepared Agent Dispatch lets your page prepare any number of agents in sequence — a directed line-up dispatched straight from the page, each carrying its own directive into motion.
OnBoard.md lets a page ship with its own onboarding written alongside it — the page arrives already knowing how to introduce itself, so whoever opens it next is met, not left guessing.

features.title: Pewter Tessera joins as a full page
features.summary: Pewter Tessera ships as a full Suite 8 page — pick a locality to preview an SCP's shipped colors without ever touching your own styling.
detail: Pewter Tessera is now a full Suite 8 page in its own right. Choose a locality and it previews that SCP's shipped colors in place — a look at how another app dresses itself, held entirely apart from your own styling. Nothing you preview ever lands on your page; your look stays yours throughout.

features.title: The bridge never hangs on git
features.summary: A remote git operation that stalls waiting for credentials can no longer freeze the bridge — it fails fast with a plain reason, and every control stays live.
detail: A push anor pull whose transport stalled awaiting a credential answer used to hold the whole bridge with it — buttons pressed into silence until a relaunch. Git is now told never to prompt (it fails immediately with its own reason instead), and a hard two-minute backstop ends any transport that stalls without prompting. The failure surfaces in the command log like any other; the bridge stays live throughout.
This is a CLI-only release — your app needs no changes. Update the bridge from the Update page and relaunch.

features.title: The update flow, reinforced
features.summary: The staging update rides a hardened circuit — any number of your SCPs at once, every failure naming its position, one gesture to finalize on whichever branch you stand.
detail: The whole circuit was reinforced in the field: concurrent updates share one source refresh instead of racing it, every SCP keeps its own update rail, and a failure lights the exact stage it stopped at with its reason — never a silent wall.

Two field-earned habits keep it smooth. Run an update with all your changes committed — the update lands on your current branch, and a clean tree is the ground the circuit expects. And if the Turn Over prompt does not appear after the resolver completes, that is a stochastic miss, not a failure: run the update again, anor tell the resolver session — “Finalize the resolution — write the pending-0 resolution file and fire the Turn Over prompt.” The apply lands the moment the resolution arrives.

features.title: Your SCPs, curated — Archive, Restore, Delete
features.summary: The install roster grows a second shelf: archive finished SCPs out of the working set, restore them intact when they matter again, and delete with a deliberate guard.
detail: The Installation page now carries two tabs — Installed and Archived. Archiving moves the whole SCP into a vault beside the working set — nothing is lost, it simply leaves the daily roster. Restore brings it back exactly as it left, git and all.

Deletion is deliberate by design: an installed SCP asks you to type its name before it goes; an archived one asks a plain yes-anor-no. The template itself is system-protected — the ground every install builds from can be neither archived nor deleted.

Work-branch worktrees are first-class citizens of the vault: a worktree SCP wears its own hatched marking, a live SCP refuses the vault until it is stopped, and the git linkage is repaired on the way in anor out so both trees stay whole. Removing an instance from the Session Manager is now one clean acknowledgment — no more stuck 'Removing…'.

features.title: Release notes that know your SCP
features.summary: The Update page now carries the release notes themselves — filtered to what YOUR SCP would actually gain, each release weighed with a magnitude, before you decide to update.
detail: Every release is recorded in a versioned manifest the bridge reads live — anor straight from your own machine in a development loop. The Update page folds it open as What this update carries: the releases your SCP has not yet landed, each with its features in full and a magnitude of one to five marking the degree of change it brings.

The filter keys on what your SCP has actually applied — not the version string — so an SCP that skipped three releases sees all three, and one that is current sees the plain release notes with nothing pending. The same notes render on the Home page as the full tour, from one shared source.

When an update is pending, the panel opens itself — the notes are the first thing you meet on the Update page. It folds away the moment the update process begins, yielding the floor to the review rail; your own toggle always wins over the automatic motion.

features.title: Updates that explain themselves
features.summary: The update diff now carries the exact preservation rules it was computed under — the resolver working inside your SCP reads the guard directly from the artifact.
detail: Every SCP update is a three-way merge guarded by preservation rules: your SCP’s identity — its name, its config — is never clobbered by a template default, and certain files are never deleted. Until now those rules lived only inside the bridge, where the resolver working inside your SCP had no way to read them. The diff is now self-describing: its provenance block pins the exact rules the merge was computed under.

The apply step prefers those pinned rules too — so the rules that computed your update are the rules that land it, even when the update itself is changing the bridge mid-flight. Smoother updates, with the guard in plain sight.

features.title: Every SCP holds its own anchor
features.summary: Sessions, anchors, and bindings are now scoped to the SCP that owns them — two SCPs can each carry the same Suite, side by side, without ever crossing.
detail: Before, a Suite’s anchor was found by NAME alone — the first match across every SCP. A fresh SCP’s page could adopt ANOTHER SCP’s session: an old, empty terminal surfacing where a new anchor belonged, a resume of a conversation that never existed, a menu authored into the wrong SCP’s files. The whole identity chain is now per-SCP: every spawn carries its own SCP’s name, every anchor claim stays within its SCP, a re-engaged session keeps its Suite identity, and a session with nothing to resume boots fresh instead of dying.

The research workers ride the same ground: a dispatched Topic Researcher now boots bare — its streamed plan IS its directive — while the page’s own anchor keeps its full onboarding, primed into motion.

features.title: Spawn plainly, anchor deliberately
features.summary: The Session Manager spawns PLAIN instances — no onboarding, no anchor claim. Anchoring belongs to the Suite’s own page, and the Suite list reads live from your SCP’s folder.
detail: The Session Manager’s two lanes are now named: Spawn General Session above, and the Suite 8 dropdown below — select a Suite to enable its spawn. A Session-Manager spawn is a plain instance: it never claims a page’s anchor and never takes the onboarding seed. The page’s own menu remains the one door that mints, anchors, and primes.

The Suite dropdown scans YOUR SCP’s own Suite folder fresh on every open — a Suite you just created appears immediately, turn-overs included. And a new chip on every Suite menu reads Anchor: Specified — your page addresses its own SCP’s anchor; the Local cross-SCP tabbing it teases is a coming refinement.

features.title: The Forge cycle, completed
features.summary: The Entourage Forge engages the moment a page is created — and the turn-over becomes the trigger at the END of its work, resolving the right branch on its own.
detail: Before, a fresh page demanded a turn-over before the Forge could even begin — and on a brand-new app with a default git tree, that demand pointed at a working branch that did not exist yet. The order is now the cycle it always meant to be: engage at creation, work, then land. The landing trigger surfaces once there is work on the tree, and the press resolves the branch itself — a fresh app takes its first turn-over with the same overlay and care as the app’s very first landing; a working branch simply restarts; an established app carries the work onto its working branch.
And git actions fired from any page now carry the app’s own name to the bridge — a push from the Release pane lands on the right repository whether or not anything ever set focus that session.

features.title: Born from the freshest template
features.summary: Creating a new app now refreshes the template to the latest release before the birth — never a stale vintage — and a one-press Create door joins SCP Management.
detail: A field catch: a new app could be born from whatever template vintage its workspace had frozen at, wearing a current version over old bones. Every template birth now refreshes to the freshest release first — the same retained comparison machinery the update circuit already trusts — falling back gracefully when offline. The staged rail says so as it works: refreshing the template, then clone, install, ready.

And creation is now a page away: Create a New SCP in SCP Management — one PascalCase name, one press, the same staged rail the manifest install walks. The TUI path is honest too: typing lands from the first key, and every character belongs to the name you are writing.

features.title: The shader stands its ground
features.summary: A render-mode choice now survives every internal rewrite — the chromatic shader no longer goes dark after a session of heavy motion.
detail: The one writer that recorded your render-mode choice could be overwritten by routine internal refreshes — the choice silently erased, the shader falling dark. Every writer now preserves the shader fields it does not own. And closing the CLI now reliably carries the whole window set down with it — no orphaned windows holding the stage.
